## Current applied collaboration

<div class="current-project"><p class="eyebrow">Active Mitacs Accelerate research</p><h3>University of Guelph × Ausable Bayfield Conservation Authority</h3><p>My current postdoctoral work connects agricultural watershed monitoring, process-based watershed modelling with IMWEBs (Integrated Modelling for Watershed Evaluation of BMPs), conservation scenarios, and practical indicators in the <a href="https://www.healthylakehuron.com/">Healthy Lake Huron</a> context. <a href="https://www.abca.ca/">ABCA</a> is the formal Mitacs partner. BMPs are beneficial management practices, such as cover crops and buffers.</p><p>The project draws on ABCA, Maitland Valley Conservation Authority, and broader Healthy Lake Huron partner data and expertise. Its intended outputs support conservation targeting, monitoring design, and clear reporting of water-quality progress.</p><a href="research.qmd#current-project-healthy-lake-huron">Explore the research example →</a></div>

## Food-System Buffer Monitoring & Anticipatory Decision-Making

<p class="eyebrow">Developing research direction · Submitted CPRA proposal</p>

Food-system buffers are capacities that help food systems absorb stress. This developing work asks how stress signals and weakening buffers can be identified early enough to inform adaptation and policy. The CPRA proposal has been submitted; it is not an awarded or funded fellowship.

<div class="framework"><ol class="framework-stages"><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">01</span><h3>Stress signals</h3><p>Environmental · Remote sensing · Market · Socio-economic · Political-institutional</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">02</span><h3>Food-system buffers</h3><p>Environmental · Market · Livelihood · Institutional · Social-political</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">03</span><h3>Situation update</h3><p>What stress is increasing? Which buffers are weakening? What remains available? Who can access it?</p></li><li><span class="step-number" aria-hidden="true">04</span><h3>Anticipatory decision</h3><p>What adaptation or policy response is still possible?</p></li></ol></div>

The proposed work is designed to engage networks connected through Arrell Food Institute and Professor Evan Fraser, including FAO, Oxford Martin School, Cornell, and the RAAPID Center (University of Maryland/NASA Harvest). These are prospective network connections for the developing work.

## Place-based research interest: Bangladesh

Bangladesh has been a long-term research and professional context for my work on water quality, environmental risk, climate adaptation, agricultural resilience, and science–policy practice. I am interested in future collaborations connecting this experience with Earth observation, GeoAI (AI for geographic data), agricultural landscape management, and food-system resilience, including comparative work between Canada and Bangladesh.
